title: ProxyMessage import-time registry — render-frame + channel_action set (CANONICAL, replaces pre-canonical)
intent: The current libs/contracts/registry.py is PRE-CANONICAL: its MessageType is {connect-repo, approve-draft, invite-proxy} plus a tile-originated approve WS path — a shape CANONICAL §12.9/§12.12 explicitly deletes (tile is outbound-only, connect moved to REST). This node rebuilds the registry to §4.1's canonical set: the single INBOUND type channel_action, and the OUTBOUND render-frame family (response.start/chunk/end, voice.speak, canvas.patch, tool.start, tile.state, note.line, draft.card). It keeps the import-time __init_subclass__/__pydantic_init_subclass__ self-registration, the assert_registry_closed() closure, and the signal-surface exclusion (§11.8), but replaces the discriminator enum + concrete models and adds the three declared maps (MESSAGE_HANDLERS: exactly-1 per inbound; MESSAGE_PROJECTORS: >=1 per outbound; MESSAGE_PRODUCERS for the field-diff). This is D-006: breaking, so every importer of ConnectRepoMessage/ApproveDraftMessage/InviteProxyMessage must be migrated.
definition_of_done: registry.py's MessageType is exactly {channel_action, response.start, response.chunk, response.end, voice.speak, canvas.patch, tool.start, tile.state, note.line, draft.card}; INBOUND={channel_action}, OUTBOUND=rest; assert_registry_closed() proves set-equality AND every inbound has exactly one handler AND every outbound has >=1 projector; the three declared maps exist; signal-surface events still excluded (§11.8) and their leak still fails. NOT done if the pre-canonical connect-repo/approve-draft/invite-proxy types survive anywhere, if any importer still references the deleted models, or if closure only checks set-equality without handler/projector coverage.
integration_point: libs/contracts/src/contracts/registry.py (replace MessageType + concrete models; extend assert_registry_closed with handler/projector coverage)
acceptance: WHEN libs.contracts is imported and assert_registry_closed() is called THE SYSTEM SHALL prove MessageType == CHANNEL_REGISTRY keys, every inbound type has exactly one handler and every outbound type has at least one projector, and raise on any missing/unhandled/unprojected type or a leaked signal-surface event.
acceptance_cmd: libs/contracts -k 'registry_closed or channel_action or render_frame or projector_coverage'

signal-surface events out of client-registry scope (§11.8)

must not re-admit a tile-originated inbound type or a connect.* WS type — both were deliberately deleted

title: ChannelAction + render-frame Pydantic models (meeting_id UUID, Field(max_length), Literal selectors)
intent: The concrete Pydantic models registered into the §4.1 registry, in a new libs/contracts/channel.py: the one inbound ChannelAction (meeting_id: UUID, surface: Literal ActionSurface no 'tile', action: closed Literal set, canvas_id: UUID|None, arg: Annotated[str|None, Field(max_length=2000)]) plus the outbound render frames (VoiceSpeak, ResponseStart/Chunk/End, CanvasPatch, ToolStart, TileState, NoteLine, DraftCard). Each is a ProxyMessage subclass so it self-registers at import. The three disciplines — meeting_id UUID (rejects attacker-shaped input before any DB lookup, making isolation sound), Field(max_length) on free text (bounds DoS), Literal closed sets on selectors (an out-of-set surface/action is a validation error, not an if/else fall-through) — are what the funnel relies on.
definition_of_done: libs/contracts/channel.py defines ChannelAction and every outbound render-frame model as registered ProxyMessage subclasses; ChannelAction.meeting_id is UUID, arg is capped at 2000, surface is ActionSurface (no 'tile'), action is the closed §4.2 Literal; a non-UUID meeting_id, an over-length arg, and an out-of-set surface/action each raise ValidationError. NOT done if any model is a hand-built dict, if 'tile' is an inbound origin, if a free-text field is uncapped, or if a selector is an open str.
integration_point: libs/contracts/src/contracts/channel.py (new module imported by libs.contracts __init__ so subclass registration fires)
acceptance: WHEN a ChannelAction is validated with a non-UUID meeting_id, an arg over 2000 chars, or a surface/action outside the closed Literal THE SYSTEM SHALL raise a ValidationError before any handler or DB lookup runs.
acceptance_cmd: libs/contracts -k 'channel_action_model or render_frame_model or meeting_id_uuid or literal_selector'
invariants: do not re-describe a shared type in prose — models live in libs/contracts (CANONICAL §11.5)
tile is outbound-only — no TileAddress inbound model
risks: arg cap + socket-level payload cap are two separate DoS bounds; this node owns the field cap, the gateway owns the socket cap
meeting_id UUID everywhere per §11.2 (operation_runs.scope_id stays text — do not conflate)

title: Typed CAPABILITIES catalog + build-time UI manifest (never fetches, service-strings never ship to browser)
intent: The single typed source of truth for what Proxy can do — a plain Python module constant CAPABILITIES: dict[str, Capability] in libs/contracts/capabilities.py (mirroring the funded sibling's AGENTS config). Each Capability declares id, user-facing label, OutputKind, renderer config, allowed Actions (surface/propose/approve), a service: binding (wake:/disposition:) for capabilities a Doc 04/05 behavior fulfills, and its surfaces. The backend imports this module directly; the UI does NOT — a build step generates a small JSON/TS manifest of {id,label,output,surfaces} only, so the internal service: strings never reach the browser (fixes the service-string-in-TS problem). There is NO runtime GET /capabilities endpoint, NO dynamic HTTP catalog, NO boot validator (all cut in §6). allowed_on(surface) is the authorization primitive the channel_action handler calls.
definition_of_done: libs/contracts/capabilities.py exposes the typed Capability model + the CAPABILITIES constant (answer_grounded, catch_me_up, build, walkthrough at minimum) with allowed_on(surface); a build step emits a UI manifest carrying only {id,label,output,surfaces} — asserted to contain NO service:/renderer backend fields; there is no runtime capabilities endpoint. NOT done if the UI imports the Python module, if a service: string appears in the generated manifest, if a GET /capabilities route exists, or if walkthrough is modeled as a disposition/delivery flag (it is a delivery MODE owned by §12.3, catalog names only the label).
integration_point: libs/contracts/src/contracts/capabilities.py (typed source) + a build step that writes the UI label manifest consumed by apps/connect + apps/tile
acceptance: WHEN the UI manifest is generated from CAPABILITIES THE SYSTEM SHALL emit only {id,label,output,surfaces} per capability and never a service: or backend renderer field, and no runtime GET /capabilities endpoint SHALL exist.
acceptance_cmd: libs/contracts -k 'capabilities_catalog or ui_manifest or no_capabilities_endpoint or allowed_on'
invariants: dynamic, never hard-coded — situation→action lives in judgment; catalog owns only surface/label config (Law 4)
user-visible strings never carry internal names (Orchestrator/Scribe/workroom) — naming lint over labels
risks: the 'what can you do?' answer (§2.4 #10) must render CAPABILITIES filtered to this repo's mounted tools — it cannot over-claim; the honesty derives from this one source
manifest is generated at build, not fetched at runtime — no drift path

title: The one dispatch funnel — rate-limit → registry-lookup → validate → meeting/entity isolation → route
intent: The single coroutine every inbound WS channel_action flows through, replacing the current 3-line stub dispatch() (which only checks is_owner and echoes the payload). It runs the ordered funnel of §4.3: (1) rate-limit per-connection via the pinned `limits`/`slowapi` in-memory backend (not a hand-rolled bucket, §11.11); (2) registry lookup by declared type; (3) Pydantic-validate once centrally (§4.2); (4) meeting/tenant isolation keyed on meeting_id PRESENCE — a handler never sees an un-isolated message, and the default-reject floor refuses a scoped message with no meeting_id; (5) entity→owner→tenant resolved from OUR store (never the client's meeting_id) killing the smuggle-a-foreign-id bug; (6) route to the exactly-one handler. Every failure returns a generic 'Not found'/'Slow down.' — never a type/tenancy leak. Auth is guaranteed at the connection upgrade (gateway), never per-message. This funnel IS the isolation guarantee that makes an unchecked route structurally impossible.
definition_of_done: libs/http/dispatch.py runs all six ordered steps; a channel_action with a foreign or absent meeting_id, an unregistered type, an oversized/malformed body, or a smuggled canvas_id owned by another meeting is refused with a generic error and NO handler runs; the rate limiter is the `limits`/`slowapi` in-memory backend keyed per-connection; auth is enforced at upgrade in the gateway (401 before the 101). NOT done if isolation is opt-in per handler, if any error message distinguishes absent-vs-foreign-tenant, if the client meeting_id is trusted to authorize an entity, or if the rate limiter is hand-rolled.
integration_point: libs/http/src/http/dispatch.py (rebuild the funnel) + libs/http/src/http/gateway.py (new: authorize_upgrade before the 101) + libs/http/src/http/handlers/channel_action.py (new: the one inbound handler)
acceptance: WHEN an inbound channel_action carries a foreign/absent meeting_id, an unregistered type, an oversized body, or a smuggled entity id THE SYSTEM SHALL refuse with a generic error and route nothing, and WHEN it is well-formed and owned THE SYSTEM SHALL validate-once, isolate, then invoke exactly one handler.
acceptance_cmd: libs/http -k 'dispatch_funnel or meeting_isolation or entity_smuggle or rate_limit or upgrade_auth or generic_error'
invariants: isolation triad — one tenant never sharing with another; runtime tripwire on cross-tenant read
human control is absolute — world-touching actions gated (Law 3)
generic error on every failure — no tenancy/type leak
risks: keeps the existing is_owner fence (§12.10) — a reclaimed process must not route a side-effecting message; fold it into the funnel, don't drop it
require_entity_access must resolve the owning meeting from OUR DB, never the client-supplied meeting_id (the smuggle bug)
WS instance-affinity: bump meeting_activity sliding-TTL keep-alive (§11.11)

title: ChannelProjector — AgentChunk delta stream → registered render frames (pure rendering, two event types)
intent: The pure-rendering projector in services/transport/projector.py that maps the delta stream to registered ProxyMessage render frames. It consumes the OUTPUT of stream_deltas (applied exactly once in BehaviorRunner.run, §11.3) — chunk.text is already a TRUE delta, forwarded as-is, NEVER re-accumulated or re-wrapped (the old Doc 08 re-wrap is deleted). Field access is chunk.type (never .kind), chunk.metadata['name'] for TOOL_USE, chunk.metadata['structured'] for TOOL_RESULT. Per AMENDMENT C2 the projector is NARROWED to two event types only: a TOOL_USE → tile 'working…' line (ToolStart) or, for a delivery tool (speak/send_chat/show_screen), the model's own streaming text delta → VoiceSpeak/ResponseChunk/CanvasPatch; a structured TOOL_RESULT → CanvasPatch. Everything else — raw TEXT, the model's reasoning — is NOT projected to any surface. The wake-turn delivery tools are the sole delivery authority (§12.3): the projector never auto-extracts a headline and never decides a channel. Every projected frame is a registered instance serialized via model_dump(); the in-process carry_turn drives it over the same delta stream every consumer reads, with the ordering law + readyState guard.
definition_of_done: services/transport/projector.py maps a delta-stream AgentChunk to registered render frames: TOOL_USE(delivery tool)→VoiceSpeak/ResponseChunk/CanvasPatch, TOOL_USE(work tool)→ToolStart, structured TOOL_RESULT→CanvasPatch, TEXT/everything-else→nothing; chunk.text is forwarded as a delta (never re-accumulated); frames are registered ProxyMessage instances and MESSAGE_PROJECTORS has an entry per outbound type; carry_turn emits ResponseStart→frames→ResponseEnd and drops on a closed connection. NOT done if it re-wraps/re-runs stream_deltas, reads .kind/.tool/.structured as top-level attrs, projects raw TEXT, or auto-extracts a headline and decides to speak.
integration_point: services/transport/src/transport/projector.py (new) + services/transport/src/transport/carrier.py (drive the projector over the delta stream)
acceptance: WHEN the projector receives a delta-stream AgentChunk THE SYSTEM SHALL emit a registered render frame ONLY for a TOOL_USE (delivery→channel frame, work→tile line) or a structured TOOL_RESULT (canvas), forward chunk.text as-is without re-accumulation, and project nothing for raw TEXT.
acceptance_cmd: services/transport -k 'projector or render_frame or no_rewrap or no_text_projection or delivery_tool_frame'
invariants: stream_deltas applied exactly once (§11.3) — consumers receive deltas, never re-wrap
delivery tools are the sole delivery authority (§12.3) — projector is pure rendering
grounded or silent — projector renders only what the wake turn delivered (Law 1)
risks: tool-input streaming shape must be confirmed against the live SDK at build (§11.10) — text_delta key on a TOOL_USE
camera↔screenshare exclusivity: screen mode-change frames are separate from CanvasPatch (§2.5)
the chat-mirror of a spoken line is a harness mirror, not a second projector decision

title: Contract-registry HTTP wrappers — protected()/PublicAuthzCtx + allowlist + route-scope test + safeError
intent: The typed HTTP wrappers in libs/http/registry.py (net-new): protected() yields an AuthzCtx{user_id, tenant_id non-null} so tenant_id is safe as a DB filter by construction; a public handler gets a PublicAuthzCtx with nullable tenant_id ON PURPOSE so it CANNOT be a DB filter by accident. A handler receives a credentials-only context and NEVER a raw Request/Response, making 'read the tenant from the body' unrepresentable. The PUBLIC_ROUTES frozenset is the only unauthenticated allowlist (webhooks/recall HMAC-gated, connect/status, connect/install/start, and GET /m/{meeting_id} dual-mode). safeError collapses every non-validation error to a per-status fallback so external callers never see an internal error (validation errors ARE returned — they describe the caller's own bad input). The structural guarantee is a route-enumeration test asserting every route is protected() or allowlisted. TRIM: skip the AST ruff-ban rule (code-review convention suffices at V0); KEEP the wrappers, safeError, the allowlist, and the route test.
definition_of_done: libs/http/registry.py exposes protected()/AuthzCtx and PublicAuthzCtx, PUBLIC_ROUTES, and safe_error_handler; a handler cannot access raw Request/Response; PublicAuthzCtx.tenant_id is nullable; safeError returns the per-status fallback for non-validation errors and the issues body for a RequestValidationError; tests/security/test_routes_are_scoped.py asserts every app route is protected() or in PUBLIC_ROUTES. NOT done if a route registers raw without a wrapper and escapes the test, if an internal error string leaks to an external caller, or if PublicAuthzCtx.tenant_id is non-null and usable as a filter.
integration_point: libs/http/src/http/registry.py (new) + libs/http/src/http/safe_error.py (new) + tests/security/test_routes_are_scoped.py; mounted on services/harness/src/control_plane/app.py
acceptance: WHEN the route-enumeration test runs THE SYSTEM SHALL assert every app route is protected()-scoped or in the PUBLIC_ROUTES allowlist, and WHEN a non-validation error escapes a handler THE SYSTEM SHALL return only a per-status fallback body.
acceptance_cmd: libs/http -k 'http_registry or protected or public_authz or safe_error or routes_are_scoped'
invariants: one authenticated surface on the connect app (§12.9)
isolation triad — tenant_id non-null-by-construction as the only safe DB filter
external callers never see an internal error
risks: PublicAuthzCtx.tenant_id nullable is load-bearing — it is the type that prevents an accidental cross-tenant read on a public route
the live cross-tenant E2E (§4.8) is KEPT and lands with the /m/ routes, not here

title: Recall webhook HMAC-signature verifier — the public route earns its exemption by proving the caller
intent: The webhook receiver in control_plane/webhooks.py durably lands a delivery (INSERT-on-conflict→200→drain) but does NOT yet verify the caller is Recall — the HMAC signature gate of §4.6 is unbuilt. This node adds libs/http/webhook.py's verify_recall_signature: a constant-time hmac.compare_digest over the raw body against settings.recall_webhook_secret, raising 401 'bad signature' on mismatch. The HMAC IS the gate — it is our equivalent of the sibling repo's 'a public route must supply a reason': a public route earns its exemption by proving the caller, not by trust. It wraps the existing durable-insert intake so the signature is checked BEFORE the row lands. The Recall webhook payload/signature-header shape is confirmed against live docs at build (§11.10), not guessed.
definition_of_done: libs/http/webhook.py exposes verify_recall_signature that computes the HMAC over the raw request body and rejects a bad/missing signature with 401 via constant-time compare, wired ahead of control_plane/webhooks.py ingest(); POST /webhooks/recall is in PUBLIC_ROUTES but only proceeds on a valid signature; the header/payload shape is confirmed against live Recall docs. NOT done if the webhook lands a row before verifying the signature, if compare is non-constant-time, or if the signature check is skippable.
integration_point: libs/http/src/http/webhook.py (new verifier) wired into services/harness/src/control_plane/webhooks.py (before the durable INSERT)
acceptance: WHEN a POST /webhooks/recall arrives with a missing or mismatched x-recall-signature THE SYSTEM SHALL reject it 401 via constant-time compare before any row lands, and WHEN the signature is valid THE SYSTEM SHALL proceed to the durable insert-then-200 intake.
acceptance_cmd: services/harness -k 'webhook_verify or recall_signature or bad_signature or hmac'
invariants: secrets only from Secret Manager, never hard-coded (recall_webhook_secret)
external callers never see an internal error
public route earns its exemption by proving the caller
risks: Recall signature header name + HMAC algorithm must be confirmed against live docs at build (§11.10)
verify BEFORE the durable insert — a forged delivery must never dedupe-poison webhook_events

title: Capability-token verifier — signed, short-TTL, meeting-scoped, revocable, read-only notes (built)
intent: libs/ops/src/ops/capability.py already implements the whole net-new security primitive: mint_capability_token + authorize over a structured (non-string) CapabilityToken signed with HMAC over {meeting_id, scope, expires_at}. It grants ONLY notes:read on its own meeting, refuses an expired/tampered/wrong-meeting token, and NEVER grants a mutation (draft:accept refused). This node VERIFIES that built code satisfies §2.8's capability-token contract: short-TTL, meeting-scoped (a token for meeting A cannot read B — meeting_id in the signed body, re-checked against the path), revocable, read-only. The one gap to confirm is the revocation path (a revoked_tokens check or per-meeting token epoch) named in §2.8 — verify it exists or flag it. The verifier is consumed by the /m/{meeting_id} read route's dual-mode branch.
definition_of_done: the built mint/authorize is confirmed to grant only notes:read on the token's own meeting with a valid signature and unexpired TTL, and to refuse every other action, any other meeting, and any expired/tampered token; the revocation mechanism (revoked check or token epoch) is confirmed present or explicitly flagged as the one net-new gap. NOT done if authorize can be coerced to grant a mutation, if a wrong-meeting token reads notes, or if revocation is silently absent without a flag.
integration_point: libs/ops/src/ops/capability.py (verify against §2.8) — consumed by the /m/{meeting_id} read route
acceptance: WHEN a capability token is presented for a different meeting, an expired TTL, a tampered signature, or any action other than notes:read THE SYSTEM SHALL refuse, and only a valid, unexpired, same-meeting notes:read token SHALL be granted.
acceptance_cmd: libs/ops -k 'capability_token or notes_read or wrong_meeting or expired or not_permitted'
invariants: human control is absolute — a token grants read-only, never a world-touching accept (Law 3)
the read-only frontier is enforced in code, not by trusting an opaque bearer blob
risks: confirm the revocation path exists (revoked_tokens or per-meeting token epoch, §2.8) — the one item most likely to be the genuine gap in the built primitive
per-process signing key is fine only because mint and authorize run in the same control_plane process

title: The connect page — GitHub App install + REST readiness poll rendering all five states (build-new)
intent: The one out-of-meeting surface: a small static Vite app (apps/connect is currently a bare scaffold) plus its two public REST routes on control_plane. It does three things and nothing else — a door, not a dashboard: (1) launch the GitHub App install flow (POST /connect/install/start, Doc 01); (2) watch it get ready via a REST status poll GET /connect/status (NOT a WS message — the connect page is REST per §12.12) that renders ALL FIVE readiness states of Doc 01's Readiness enum: connecting → cloning → indexing → ready, plus an explicit not_ready terminal state that names the gaps (gaps: list[str]); the happy path shows the honest coverage number and flagged files ('94% indexed · 12 files flagged: generated'); (3) invite instructions. There is no 'mapping' state (indexing = clone + tree-sitter + LSP + dep-graph). Readiness is the first trust moment — showing the honest number is the brand working before any meeting. Both routes are public but validated by the §4.6 wrappers (HMAC/allowlist), because the connect page is a public URL.
definition_of_done: apps/connect renders the teal connect page with the install flow and the invite instructions; GET /connect/status (public, allowlisted) polls Doc 01's readiness and the UI renders all five states connecting|cloning|indexing|ready|not_ready(+gaps) with the real coverage_pct and flagged files on the happy path and named gaps on not_ready; POST /connect/install/start launches the install. NOT done if any readiness state is missing (especially not_ready+gaps), if the coverage number is faked, if a 'mapping' state appears, or if the poll is a WS message instead of REST.
acceptance: WHEN a repo is connecting THE SYSTEM SHALL render each of the five readiness states connecting|cloning|indexing|ready|not_ready with the honest coverage number and flagged files on ready and named gaps on not_ready, via the public REST poll.
acceptance_cmd: services/harness -k 'connect_status or readiness_states or not_ready_gaps or connect_install'
invariants: grounded or silent — show the real coverage number, name what is missing, never pretend (Law 1)
never overstate — coverage is a lower-bound-honest number, not a claim (Law 2)
connect page is a public URL — validated like any public API
risks: connect page moved to REST — do NOT re-introduce connect.* WS registry entries (§12.12)
the five states map to Doc 01's Readiness enum exactly (§1.5) — not_ready is a real terminal state, not an error page

title: GET /m/{meeting_id} home — dual-mode read (session OR capability token): notes + staged-draft cards
intent: The per-meeting home — the flagship's missing home, closing F1 (the notes artifact has a home) + F9 (drafts have an accept surface). GET /m/{meeting_id} is dual-mode: a signed-in tenant member takes it protected() (server-side meeting→tenant check; anyone else gets Not found), OR a non-signed-in forwarded-to recipient presents a capability token for a READ-ONLY notes view (token = notes only, NO drafts). It renders the §2.6 notes markdown folded server-side from note_deltas via the existing GET /internal/notes/{meeting_id} reader (§11.4), PLUS that meeting's staged_drafts cards (§2.4 #8) for the authenticated view. It lives on the control_plane app so it reuses that app's auth wall and transport — net new is 1 page + this read route (the mutations are a separate node). It is deliberately not a dashboard: one meeting's notes + drafts, addressable by its meeting_id UUID.
definition_of_done: GET /m/{meeting_id} on control_plane renders the §2.6 notes (folded from note_deltas via /internal/notes) + that meeting's staged_drafts cards for a signed-in tenant member; a valid capability token yields a notes-only view with NO drafts; a wrong tenant / no session / no token yields Not found; the route is in PUBLIC_ROUTES (public only via a valid token). NOT done if a token exposes drafts, if a cross-tenant member reads the meeting, if notes are read from anywhere but the folded note_deltas reader, or if it grows a cross-meeting list/analytics/history.
integration_point: services/harness/src/control_plane/meeting_home.py (new: GET /m/{meeting_id}) + apps/connect (the /m/ page) — mounted on control_plane/app.py
acceptance: WHEN a signed-in tenant member opens GET /m/{meeting_id} THE SYSTEM SHALL render the §2.6 notes + that meeting's staged-draft cards; WHEN a capability token is presented THE SYSTEM SHALL render notes only with no drafts; WHEN neither authorizes the meeting THE SYSTEM SHALL return Not found.
acceptance_cmd: services/harness -k 'meeting_home or m_read or token_notes_only or cross_tenant_not_found'
invariants: one authenticated surface on the connect app (§12.9)
isolation triad — meeting→tenant checked server-side; token never reads another meeting
human control is absolute — token grants read-only, drafts never exposed to it (Law 3)
risks: dual-mode: the token path must NOT return drafts (drafts = [] when grant present)

title: POST /m/{meeting_id}/drafts/{draft_id}/{accept,reject} — CSRF + tenant + idempotent + audit, calls Doc 04 accept
intent: control_plane/accept.py already reads the DURABLE staged_drafts row (post-teardown safe, never the dead review_session) and marks it accepted — but it is NOT yet the §2.8 HTTP mutation route: it lacks the protected() wall, the server-side meeting/draft→tenant check, CSRF, idempotency, audit, and the reject symmetry. This node FIXES it into the two strictly-protected() routes: POST .../accept and .../reject, each with a server-side require_meeting_and_draft_in_tenant check + CSRF + idempotent + audit, calling Doc 04's accept/reject handler (notes-edit apply for a core edit; a code-change draft RECORDS approval and exposes the diff bundle for download, never pushes — §12.9). The draft card (§2.4 #8) posts the persisted Envelope.draft_id here. These routes are NEVER in PUBLIC_ROUTES and never reachable by a capability token.
definition_of_done: POST /m/{meeting_id}/drafts/{draft_id}/accept and .../reject are protected()-only, run a server-side meeting/draft→tenant check + CSRF + idempotency + audit, and call Doc 04's accept/reject handler reading the durable staged_drafts row; a code-change draft records approval and exposes the diff bundle but never pushes; a replayed accept is idempotent; a capability token cannot reach either route. NOT done if either route is allowlisted, reachable by token, missing CSRF/idempotency/audit, trusts the client meeting_id, or pushes a code-change.
integration_point: services/harness/src/control_plane/accept.py (fix into the two protected routes) + services/harness/src/control_plane/meeting_home.py — mounted on control_plane/app.py
acceptance: WHEN a tenant member POSTs a valid CSRF accept for a draft in their meeting THE SYSTEM SHALL idempotently apply via Doc 04's accept handler and audit it; WHEN the request lacks CSRF, crosses a tenant, or presents a capability token THE SYSTEM SHALL refuse.
acceptance_cmd: services/harness -k 'accept_route or reject_route or csrf or idempotent_accept or draft_tenant or no_push'
invariants: human control is absolute — accept is a human click on a staged draft; core apply is a code-change draft, never a push (Law 3, §12.9)
reads the durable staged_drafts row, never the dead in-memory review_session
isolation triad — meeting/draft→tenant checked server-side, never the client meeting_id
risks: idempotency: a replayed accept (double-click, retry) must be a no-op, not a double-apply
the accept posts the persisted Envelope.draft_id (§11.5) — the card and the route read the same typed field
audit row is a hard requirement — a world-touching action is recorded

title: The tile — orb bloom + §2.2 state machine, each state bound to a real system event (no state without a source)
intent: The tile is one HTML/canvas page (Doc 02's canvas, apps/tile is a bare scaffold) streamed as Proxy's camera: the presence orb (a soft breathing bloom in teal-ink #35c2b8 on near-black) plus a state machine with EXACTLY the §2.2 states — listening, listening-to, working, checking(ACK), has-something, speaking, muted, reaction — each bound to its named driving system event: Doc 04 session state / name-gate + roster (listening-to caption), Doc 05 progress envelopes (working line, checking ACK ≤500ms), Doc 04 turn boundary (has-something = V0's raise-a-hand), Doc 02 mute/speaking signals. Build rule: NO state without a real source — a state that can't name its driving event does not exist. The hard ceiling: the renderer contains NO code path for facial features, character animation, or theatrical effects — the identity cannot drift into a costume because the costume is unrenderable; the orb's entire range is breath rate, firmness, shimmer, dim, pulse. The accessibility law: every tile state is ALSO carried in speech or chat (motion is an enhancement, never the only channel). The tile is OUTBOUND-ONLY: it authenticates its render WS via a meeting-scoped bearer token in the Recall URL and never originates a message.
definition_of_done: apps/tile renders the breathing teal orb and a state machine with exactly the eight §2.2 states, each driven by its named system event (tile.state frames from the projector/Doc 04/Doc 02); the renderer has no code path for faces/character-animation/theatrical effects; each state's substance is also carried in speech or chat; the render WS authenticates via the meeting-scoped bearer token and the tile sends nothing inbound. NOT done if a state has no driving event, if the renderer can draw a face/effect, if a state's substance is motion-only (accessibility law), or if the tile originates any WS message. Per the accessibility law (§2.2): every tile state is ALSO carried in speech or chat — a screen-reader/dial-in participant never loses substance; testable that every tile.state has a chat/voice fallback.
integration_point: apps/tile/* (Vite canvas app) — rendered into the call via Doc 02's Output Media; consumes tile.state render frames over the meeting-scoped render WS
acceptance: WHEN a system event fires (session live, name detected, progress envelope, turn boundary, mute/speaking) THE SYSTEM SHALL drive the corresponding §2.2 tile state, carry its substance in speech/chat too, and render no state that lacks a real driving event.
acceptance_cmd: apps/tile -k 'tile_state_machine or state_has_source or no_face_path or accessibility_dual_channel or outbound_only'
invariants: dynamic, never hard-coded — no state without a real driving event (Law 4)
talk-and-glance — the tile is glanceable, nothing to install mid-meeting (Law 5)
accessibility law — motion is an enhancement, never the only channel; tile is outbound-only (§12.9)
risks: the hard ceiling is structural: the renderer must have NO code path for faces/effects — verify by absence, not by a config flag
checking(ACK) fires ≤500ms for an LSP-bound direct answer (§12.8) — the ACK is not the spoken answer
detail belongs on the screen, ambience on the tile — the tile never carries small text the room must read (§2.5)

title: Deterministic chat formatters — decision/action note-lines, correction ack, draft card, reconciliation card
intent: The one template set of deterministic chat formatters, versioned with the §2.1 copy guide, each riding existing exhaust — NOT a wake, NEVER model-generated (so free, race-free, cannot hallucinate a decision). The decision/action note-lines (§2.4 #3) are a deterministic harness formatter keyed on a COMMITTED note_delta (§12.12) — '— noted: decision — ship Friday (Priya, Sam agreed)' / '— action: Sam → fix the retry test (by Fri)' — never spoken, honoring the session disable ('stop posting decision notes'). The correction ack (§2.4 #4) — '— corrected: ship Friday' — rides Doc 03's live notes patch. The draft card (§2.4 #8) renders what-it-is → one-line change summary → the /m/{meeting_id} link (never a raw GCS URI) → 'approve = your click', carrying the persisted Envelope.draft_id (§11.5). The reconciliation card (§2.4 #14) is a render VARIANT of the pin-to-source/draft-card renderer — two values side by side, each with its as-of source and date — riding Doc 03's contradiction-across-time detection (no new machinery). Every string is in the §2.1 copy voice (no 'As an AI', no filler, no exclamation marks, numbers over adjectives). These emit as registered NoteLine/DraftCard render frames.
definition_of_done: the formatters emit deterministic chat lines keyed on committed note_deltas (decision/action), a correction ack on a notes patch, a draft card (what/change/─/m/ link/'your click', carrying Envelope.draft_id), and a reconciliation card (two as-of-sourced values side by side) as registered NoteLine/DraftCard frames; none is a wake or model-generated; the decision/action lines honor the session disable; every string passes the naming lint + copy-voice rules. NOT done if any line is model-generated, if the draft-card link is a raw GCS URI, if a decision line ignores the session disable, or if a string carries an internal name/filler/exclamation.
integration_point: services/transport/src/transport/chat.py (formatters) + a harness formatter keyed on committed note_deltas — emits NoteLine/DraftCard frames via the projector
acceptance: WHEN a note_delta is committed THE SYSTEM SHALL deterministically emit the matching decision/action chat line (honoring the session disable, never a wake), and WHEN a staged draft or a cross-time contradiction is present THE SYSTEM SHALL render the draft card (with the /m/ link + Envelope.draft_id) or the reconciliation card.
acceptance_cmd: services/transport -k 'note_line or decision_line or correction_ack or draft_card or reconciliation_card or copy_voice'
invariants: dynamic, never hard-coded — but the note-lines are deterministic formatters, never a wake, cannot hallucinate a decision (§12.12)
user-visible strings never carry internal names; §2.1 copy voice (naming lint)
draft-card link points at /m/ authenticated home, never a raw GCS URI
risks: decision/action lines are a harness formatter keyed on a committed note_delta — NOT a projector-of-AgentChunk path (do not model-generate them)
reconciliation card is a render variant of the existing card renderer (§2.4 #14), not new machinery
the spoken-is-also-posted chat mirror is a harness mirror, not a second delivery decision

title: Per-field produce/consume contract diff — flags a field produced by one side, consumed by neither (CI, un-trimmed)
intent: The cheap Pydantic produce/consume field-diff that runs in CI NOW (un-trimmed, §11.11 + §4.8) — beyond the §4.1 set-equality (type-registered ↔ model-exists), it walks each contract model's fields over MESSAGE_PRODUCERS and flags any field produced by one side and consumed by neither. This project already PROVED field-level drift happens — the AgentChunk .kind→.type seam, the envelope verified|draft→EnvelopeStatus, the dm?→dm_available field — so we pay the small cost up front rather than wait for it to bite. The assert_fields_consumed(produced, consumed) primitive already exists in registry.py returning the orphan list; this node builds the CI gate that populates produced/consumed from the real contract models + producer registry and fails the build on a non-empty return, naming each orphan field.
definition_of_done: a CI test walks the contract models' fields via MESSAGE_PRODUCERS/consumers and fails the build (naming each orphan) when a field is produced by one side and consumed by neither; the AgentChunk/envelope/channel-report drift cases it was designed for are caught by construction. NOT done if the diff only checks set-equality (type↔model) without field-level coverage, if it is trimmed, or if it does not name the offending field.
integration_point: libs/contracts/src/contracts/registry.py (assert_fields_consumed already present) + a CI test that populates produced/consumed from the real models
acceptance: WHEN a contract field is produced by one side and consumed by neither THE SYSTEM SHALL fail the CI build and name the orphan field (signal.field produced but never consumed).
acceptance_cmd: libs/contracts -k 'field_diff or fields_consumed or produce_consume or orphan_field'
invariants: contracts — a field produced but never consumed fails the build (§11.11, un-trimmed)
do not re-describe a shared type's shape in prose — the diff runs over the real models
risks: un-trimmed per §11.11 — do NOT skip this as an optional; it is explicitly kept because field drift already bit this project
populate produced/consumed from the real producer registry, not a hand-maintained list (which would itself drift)

title: V0 screen renders (structured-progress / pin-to-source / final-artifact-preview) + human-activated walkthrough/screen-share
intent: Realizes Doc 08 §2.5: the three V0 screen render modes — structured-progress-view (the live task/plan progress), pin-to-source (a citation pinned to its file:line source), and final-artifact-preview (the completed artifact) — plus the §2.4 #12,13 human-activated controls for verbal-walkthrough and screen-share. Screen content is a render surface driven by the workroom envelope and shown via the transport show-screen verb; it is activated by a human, never auto-pushed.
definition_of_done: DONE: the three §2.5 render modes each draw from a real workroom.envelope (structured-progress from the plan/step state, pin-to-source from a citation's file:line, final-artifact-preview from the finished artifact) and render only via transport.show_screen; verbal-walkthrough and screen-share are gated behind an explicit human activation (never auto-started). NOT done: a screen mode auto-pushed without human activation, a render with no backing envelope data, or a mode that fabricates content not present in the envelope.
integration_point: new services/harness/src/control_plane/screen_modes.py, rendered over the transport show-screen verb
acceptance: WHEN a human activates a screen render (structured-progress / pin-to-source / final-artifact-preview / walkthrough / screen-share) THE SYSTEM SHALL render it from the backing workroom envelope over the show-screen verb and never auto-push it.
acceptance_cmd: services/harness/tests -k screen_content_modes or pin_to_source or final_artifact_preview
invariants: Law 3 human-activated (no auto screen-push)
Law 5 talk-and-glance (screen is optional, substance also in speech/chat)
Law 1 grounded (render only what the envelope holds)
risks: auto-pushing a screen mode
rendering fabricated/absent envelope content
walkthrough/screen-share starting without human activation

title: Copy guide CI check (banned patterns) + three honesty shapes + seed-string artifact
intent: Realizes Doc 08 §2.1/§2.3: a CI banned-pattern check enforcing the copy laws (no "As an AI", no filler, no exclamation-theatre) alongside the naming lint, plus the three honesty shapes Proxy must be able to speak (recuse / unknown / partial) and the seed-string artifact that fixes the canonical voice strings. This is a build-time guard on user-visible copy, not a runtime path.
definition_of_done: DONE: a CI check fails the build on any banned pattern in user-visible copy ("As an AI", filler phrases, exclamation-theatre), the three honesty shapes (recuse / unknown / partial) are present as canonical seed strings, and the seed-string artifact is checked in and referenced by the copy check — run alongside lint.naming. NOT done: a check that only warns, a banned pattern that slips through, a missing honesty shape, or the seed strings not being the single source the check reads.
integration_point: new libs/ops/src/lint/copy_guide.py, run in CI alongside the naming lint
acceptance: WHEN CI runs the copy guide over user-visible strings THE SYSTEM SHALL fail on any banned pattern and confirm the three honesty shapes exist as canonical seed strings.
acceptance_cmd: libs/ops/tests -k copy_guide or banned_patterns or honesty_shapes
invariants: Law 2 never-overstate (honesty shapes recuse/unknown/partial)
naming/copy laws enforced by a CI guard, not convention
risks: banned pattern slipping past the check
check that only warns instead of failing
seed strings drifting from the check's source
